BiblicalUsage: Nergal is the god the men of Cuth bring with them when they are settled in Samaria after the northern kingdom falls. He is one of the idols set up in the land, a foreign god carried in by a foreign people.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that imported gods never belong in God's land — Nergal arrived with strangers, and he never had any right to be worshipped there.
